name: The Jelutong Tree of KL Tower

location.address: Menara Kuala Lumpur (KL Tower), 2 Jalan Punchak, off Jalan P. Ramlee, Bukit Nanas, 50250 Kuala Lumpur

access: Free to view in the outdoor lobby/pedestrian mall area of KL Tower, reached by the free shuttle from the main gate; the tower's observation deck itself needs a paid ticket from about MYR 25.
transport: Bukit Nanas Monorail station, about 10 minute walk uphill
verify_notes: Standing Jelutong (Dyera costulata) preserved inside the grounds of KL Tower/Menara Kuala Lumpur, at Bukit Nanas Forest Reserve, the last patch of primary rainforest inside the KL city limits (gazetted 1906). When the tower was built (completed 1996), the design was shifted and a retaining wall built around the tree at a cost reported as RM430,000 so it would not be cut down; the tree now grows beside the pedestrian walkway near the lobby entrance. Age reported inconsistently across sources: wanderlog says '95-year-old', nerdnomads and others say 'over 100 years old' -- kept broad and vague rather than picking one. No register or arborist survey found giving girth; do not invent one. Location coordinates used are KL Tower's building address (approximate), not a tree-level GPS fix -- I could not find a published lat/long for the tree itself, only photographic and descriptive confirmation it stands beside the lobby/pedestrian mall. Species confirmed both by an Alamy stock photo captioned 'Jelutong tree (Dyera costulata) at KL Tower, Bukit Nanas' and by multiple travel-site descriptions. Flagged because sources are travel/tourism sites rather than an official DBKL or KL Tower heritage designation document; I could not find DBKL's own heritage-tree list (593 trees reported city-wide per a 2020 Selangorkini article) published anywhere online to cross-check against.
